title: prefill/decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage overlap scheduling optimizations
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: long-prefill workloads (long context windows, multi-turn chat with large system prompts) expose a latency/throughput tradeoff in the prefill->decode pipeline. Large monolithic prefill kernels block decode startup and amplify KV cache pressure. This change implements three complementary optimizations: 1) chunked prefill: split long prefill sequences into configurable chunks so decode can begin sooner; 2) speculative prefill: lightweight heuristic that proactively computes KV cache for likely next-token prefixes (based on n-gram/backoff scoring and model-conditional logits sampling) to reduce speculative decode stalls; 3) stage-overlap scheduler: runtime scheduler that co-schedules prefill-chunk execution and decode tokens on the same GPU using a windowed KV cache locking protocol and kernel priority hints to avoid memory thrashing. Design notes: chunking is implemented as a prefill splitter producing prefill-chunk tasks with metadata for sequence offsets; speculative prefill runs with a bounded speculative_budget per request and uses the same KV cache format but tags entries as speculative so they can be evicted/rolled back if mismatched; the scheduler maintains a small token-availability ring that lets decode tasks pull from prefills as soon as the first chunk is produced. Kernel selection and stream assignment changes were made so short decode kernels get a higher priority CUDA stream and large prefill kernels are placed on a best-effort stream when overlap is enabled. Backwards compatibility: all features are behind runtime flags and per-model config entries. Benchmarks: synthetic chat workload (avg prefill 2.2k tokens, decode 60 tokens) shows p50/p95/p99 latency improvements of ~8/12/18% respectively and sustained throughput gain of 8-12% at target batch sizes; memory overhead of speculative prefill is configurable and typically under 6% of total KV size for our default budget. Testing: unit tests for chunking logic, speculative tagging and rollback, scheduler invariants; e2e perf tests added to perf-canary harness; integration tests for KV cache correctness in redwood-quickstarts container. Rollout: gated rollout via feature flag + canary on perf-canary followed by staged rollout to dedicated pools; default is off for existing customers. Risks and mitigations: speculative prefill could introduce wasted compute - bounded by speculative_budget and mitigated by telemetry and automatic throttle when hit-rates are low; scheduler heuristics tuned to avoid GPU memory thrash and kernel contention. Related work: builds on earlier prefill/decode overlap PRs (see linked PRs) and integrates with continuous batching and KV cache eviction strategies. Documentation: updated runtime config docs and a short note in redwood-docs about feature flags and knobs.

review_conversation: Priya Shah (reviewer): Can you explain how speculative entries are invalidated on mismatch?

Ethan Park (author): Speculative entries are tagged and stored alongside confirmed KV entries. On mismatch we issue a compact-and-replace operation which is O(#speculative_chunks) and bounded by speculative_budget; there's a rollback path that publishes a metric for throttle heuristics.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Scheduler looks complex - how do we prevent starvation of background tasks?

Ethan Park (author): We enforce a token-window fairness policy and a backpressure token that demotes prefill chunks after N missed grants; added unit tests and a stress test in perf-canary to validate no-starvation under mixed workloads.
Mei Chen (approver): Verified e2e perf numbers on our canary cluster and sanity-checked KV correctness. Approving after small nits addressed.
